content:
I found the following code in mathlib.

/-- `SubsemiringClass S R` states that `S` is a type of subsets `s ⊆ R` that
are both a multiplicative and an additive submonoid. -/
class SubsemiringClass (S : Type*) (R : outParam (Type u)) [NonAssocSemiring R]
  [SetLike S R] : Prop extends SubmonoidClass S R, AddSubmonoidClass S R

/-- `SubmonoidClass S M` says `S` is a type of subsets `s ≤ M` that contain `1`
and are closed under `(*)` -/
class SubmonoidClass (S : Type*) (M : outParam Type*) [MulOneClass M] [SetLike S M] : Prop
    extends MulMemClass S M, OneMemClass S M

/-- `MulMemClass S M` says `S` is a type of sets `s : Set M` that are closed under `(*)` -/
class MulMemClass (S : Type*) (M : outParam Type*) [Mul M] [SetLike S M] : Prop where
  /-- A substructure satisfying `MulMemClass` is closed under multiplication. -/
  mul_mem : ∀ {s : S} {a b : M}, a ∈ s → b ∈ s → a * b ∈ s

/-- A subsemiring of a semiring `R` is a subset `s` that is both a multiplicative and an additive
submonoid. -/
structure Subsemiring (R : Type u) [NonAssocSemiring R] extends Submonoid R, AddSubmonoid R

/-- A submonoid of a monoid `M` is a subset containing 1 and closed under multiplication. -/
structure Submonoid (M : Type*) [MulOneClass M] extends Subsemigroup M where
  /-- A submonoid contains `1`. -/
  one_mem' : (1 : M) ∈ carrier

/-- A subsemigroup of a magma `M` is a subset closed under multiplication. -/
structure Subsemigroup (M : Type*) [Mul M] where
  /-- The carrier of a subsemigroup. -/
  carrier : Set M
  /-- The product of two elements of a subsemigroup belongs to the subsemigroup. -/
  mul_mem' {a b} : a ∈ carrier → b ∈ carrier → a * b ∈ carrier

My understanding (expressed in Java's terminology):

  • SubsemiringClass, SubmonoidClass, MulMemClass are interfaces.
  • Subsemiring, Submonoid, Subsemigroup are concrete classes that implement these interfaces.

There is also:

@[to_additive]
instance : MulMemClass (Subsemigroup M) M where mul_mem := fun {_ _ _} => Subsemigroup.mul_mem' _

Read: we prove that the structure Subsemigroup satisfies the interface MulMemClass.
(in Java, such proof goes inside the class, marked with @Override)

However, it seems like there is code duplication: for example, between

{a b : M}, a ∈ s → b ∈ s → a * b ∈ s

and

{a b} : a ∈ carrier → b ∈ carrier → a * b ∈ carrier

It's possible to make a helper function that takes in the set (s or carrier) and return the prop type, but it seems like it is considered not worth it?

In the opposite direction of the instance, there's ofClass that converts a typeclass instance to the sub-object structure.

Meanwhile there are Subalgebra and IntermediateField, but not their corresponding class version. Would it be fine to add one, or we would rather having some more generic mechanism than “duplicating code” all over like this?

For Subalgebra, you should use SubsemiringClass and docs#SMulMemClass in conjunction. I'm not sure how useful it would be to have a class version of IntermediateField, but I think "not very". Do you have a structure which extends docs#IntermediateField ?
My understanding is that the classes are only used to prevent duplication of things like membership lemmas. Theorem statements generally shouldn't contain .ofClass, for instance.

Actually I misread: the typeclass applies to the _type_ of the thing, not the thing itself. So you have SubsemiringClass (Subsemiring R) R, but not SubsemiringClass r R where r : Subsemiring R. Still, the duplication looks a bit weird I guess.

user202729 said:

It's possible to make a helper function that takes in the set (s or carrier) and return the prop type, but it seems like it is considered not worth it?

I think it has been considered before to write something like

structure IsMulClosed [SetLike S R] [Mul R] (s : S) : Prop where
  mul_mem {a b : M} : a ∈ s → b ∈ s → a * b ∈ s

structure IsMulOneClosed [SetLike S R] [MulOneClass R] (s : S) : Prop extends IsMulClosed s where
  one_mem : 1 ∈ s

-- ...

structure SubSemigroup [Mul M] where
  carrier : Set M
  isMulClosed : IsMulClosed carrier

structure Submonoid [MulOneClass M] where
  carrier : Set M
  isMulOneClosed : IsMulOneClosed carrier

-- ...

class MulMemClass (S : Type*) (M : outParam Type*) [Mul M] [SetLike S M] : Prop where
  isMulClosed (s : S) : IsMulClosed s

but this is a little bit annoying as you no longer get Submonoid.toSemigroup for free

I think keeping definitions concrete works out much better in practice once you start thinking about operations on the objects: lattice ops, map, comap, etc
We are currently in the middle of a long and messy refactor to make certain operations like RingHom.ker concrete rather than relying on these typeclasses

Okay, I think there was a lot of misunderstand by me yesterday confusing between the type and elements of the type, and other similar sort.

What do you think about:

class SubsemiringClass' (S : Type v) (R : outParam (Type u)) [NonAssocSemiring R]
    [SetLike S R] : Prop where
  h : ∀ s : S, ∃ t : Subsemiring R, (s : Set R) = t.carrier

I suppose the advantage is you don't need code duplication in the definition. You probably still want to prove things like mul_mem as theorems.

I suppose that's a possible way to redefine the class. I haven't thought about whether it's a good idea or not. I feel like it's not, because this way you can't make the classes extend each other and so you need to manually prove the instances connecting the heirarchy.

My feeling is it shouldn't be that bad because you already have instance like {R : Type*} [Subsemiring R] : Submonoid R which you can reuse. I'll see.

By the way, how do you think the propositional version above compare with say toSubsemiring (s : S) : {t : Subsemiring R // (s : Set R) = t.carrier}? I assume no difference if SubsemiringClass : Prop is kept because of proof irrelevance. This way is perhaps more Lean-centric.

My feeling is it shouldn't be that bad because you already have instance like {R : Type*} [Subsemiring R] : Submonoid R which you can reuse. I'll see.

The instances aren't hard to prove - but they're no longer automatic.

Perhaps one advantage is shorter code at places like this.

 instance : SubmonoidClass (Submonoid M) M where
-  one_mem := Submonoid.one_mem'
-  mul_mem {s} := s.mul_mem'
+  exists_submonoid s := ⟨s, rfl⟩

The instance could be defined like this. Just 2 lines per instance.

variable {S : Type u} {R : Type v} [NonAssocSemiring R] [SetLike S R] [h : SubsemiringClass S R]

instance : SubmonoidClass S R where
  exists_submonoid := mapCarrierWitness Subsemiring.toSubmonoid h.exists_subsemiring

With this helper.

theorem mapCarrierWitness {S : Type u} {R : Type v} [SetLike S R]
    {A B : Type v} [SetLike A R] [SetLike B R]
    (f : A → B) (h : ∀ s : S, ∃ a : A, (s : Set R) = (a : Set R))
    (hf : ∀ a, (f a : Set R) = (a : Set R) := by intro; rfl) (s : S):
    ∃ b : B, (s : Set R) = (b : Set R) := by
  obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := h s
  use f a
  rw [ha, ← hf a]

[semi-LLM-generated code, but it seems like there's only one way to write this anyway]

I think this is conceptually worse. Rather than having SubfooClass keep track of membership closure properties, it's now tied to the concrete objects themselves. I also just think it results in worse code.
Here's an idea: what goes wrong if we unbundle the SubfooClass back down into OneMemClass, AddMemClass, etc? Is it a performance hit?
@user202729 I would push hard against defining SubfooClass in terms of Subfoo witnesses, for all the reasons Artie Khovanov has articulated. I suggest abandoning this approach.

Artie Khovanov said:

Here's an idea: what goes wrong if we unbundle the SubfooClass back down into OneMemClass, AddMemClass, etc? Is it a performance hit?

This is not unreasonable, and in fact we have already started doing this to some extent. For example, there is no StarAlgHomClass, there is just AlgHomClass and StarHomClass, and we've unbundled some algebraic and topological classes (although we still have docs#ContinuousLinearMapClass). If you want to attempt an unbundling, I would be interested, and I suspect the performance would not be terrible.

Modulo performance, I think it would be good morally, to emphasise to those less familiar with the library that these classes really are just used for deduplicating things like membership lemmas. I remember making classes for my new algebraic objects for no reason when I started out 2 years ago.
Alternatively, this should be documented somewhere.

Hm. For a monoid M, conceptually I think of a SubmonoidClass S M as saying

for every s : S, s is a submonoid of M

instead of

for every s : S, s is a subset of M, 1 ∈ s and s is closed under multiplication

The ∀∃ form is pretty close to the former statement (“s is equal to a submonoid of M”), no? Why do you think it's conceptually worse?

(the class name says Submonoid, and “is a submonoid of M” is just a short way in mathematical English to say “is a subset of M containing 1 and closed under multiplication”. Though there's a little room for confusion here from type theory where M is a type while s is just a set)

I'm saying that this is the wrong way to think of this class, because we don't use the map Submonoid.ofClass in definitions, because that leads to coercion hell. The right way to think of this class is as a deduplicator of one_mem and mul_mem theorems.
https://loogle.lean-lang.org/?q=Submonoid.ofClass

user202729 said:

The ∀∃ form is pretty close to the former statement (“s is equal to a submonoid of M”), no? Why do you think it's conceptually worse?

Regardless of the conceptualization of this idea (although Artie has a point that we should not be encouraging users to use docs#Submonoid.ofClass everywhere), what we care about here is implementation, and I'm saying that ∃ s : Submonoid M, ... is the wrong one in terms of implementation.
Yeah both things are true

I would say the ∀∃ form produces worse code

class SubsemiringClass' (S : Type*) (R : outParam (Type*)) [NonAssocSemiring R]
    [SetLike S R] : Prop where
  h : ∀ s : S, ∃ t : Subsemiring R, (s : Set R) = t.carrier

variable (R S : Type*) [NonAssocSemiring R] [SetLike S R]

def SubsemiringClass.toSemiring' [SubsemiringClass S R] : S → Subsemiring R := fun s =>
  { carrier := s
    mul_mem' := MulMemClass.mul_mem
    one_mem' := OneMemClass.one_mem s
    add_mem' := AddMemClass.add_mem
    zero_mem' := ZeroMemClass.zero_mem s}

def SubsemiringClass'.toSemiring [SubsemiringClass' S R] : S → Subsemiring R := fun s =>
  { carrier := s
    mul_mem' := by
      obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := SubsemiringClass'.h s
      rw [ht]
      exact t.mul_mem'
    one_mem' := by
      obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := SubsemiringClass'.h s
      rw [ht]
      exact t.one_mem'
    add_mem' := by
      obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := SubsemiringClass'.h s
      rw [ht]
      exact t.add_mem'
    zero_mem' := by
      obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := SubsemiringClass'.h s
      rw [ht]
      exact t.zero_mem' }
